papers.abstract: We develop a method for constructing differential equations for Feynman integrals directly from multivariate intersection numbers, without fibration. The large-$\varepsilon$ expansion of the intersection pairing, with $\varepsilon$ the dimensional regulator, is given by Saito's higher residue pairings, which localise at the critical points of a potential and admit closed multivariate formulae. In the Lee-Pomeransky representation, applying these formulae to Feynman integrals requires analytic regulators $\delta$ on the coordinate hyperplanes, and the physical limit $\delta \to 0$ is not manifest. Assuming that the regulated critical points are analytic in $\delta$, we show that, as $\delta \to 0$, they organise into sectors labelled by sets of pinched propagators. We derive closed formulae for the leading and first subleading higher residue pairings in this limit, written entirely in terms of unregulated sector data. These suffice to reconstruct differential systems at most linear in $\varepsilon$, including canonical ones, bypassing integration-by-parts identities. We apply the method to the massless planar four-point ladder families up to four loops and obtain their canonical differential equations, which are new at four loops.

papers.title: Description of the decay $ ^+^-$ in the NJL chiral quark model
papers.abstract: The doubly suppressed decay $\phi \to \pi^+\pi^-$ is described in the chiral NJL quark model. This decay occurs in violation of the OZI rule and isotopic invariance. Two possible channels are considered. The first channel involves $\phi-\omega$ mixing and the subsequent decay of $\omega \to \pi^+\pi^-$. In the second channel, the decay occurs via an intermediate $\rho$ meson.

papers.title: Softer charged-hadron spectra in Ne+Ne than in O+O collisions at the same multiplicity at $s_ NN = 5.36$ TeV
papers.abstract: Charged-hadron spectra measured by the ATLAS Collaboration in O+O and Ne+Ne collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV are compared at the same charged-particle multiplicity instead of at the same centrality, to test whether the shape of the transverse-momentum spectrum at a given multiplicity depends on the size of the colliding system. At equal multiplicity, Ne+Ne collisions have a lower mean transverse momentum $\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$ than O+O collisions. Without any spectral fit, the published $\langle p_{\rm T}\rangle$ values give a Ne+Ne/O+O ratio of 0.9822 at 3-4% centrality, 6.6 standard deviations below unity even if the O+O systematic uncertainties are taken as uncorrelated between centrality classes. At $0.4 < p_{\rm T} < 2$ GeV the Ne+Ne spectrum is described by the O+O spectrum with the transverse-momentum axis compressed by a single stretch factor, $\lambda_{\rm Ne/O} = 0.969$ in the 3-4% class. It lies 9.5 or 3.3 standard deviations below unity, depending on whether the common part of the O+O systematic uncertainties cancels between centrality classes. This ordering is expected if Ne+Ne collisions have a larger transverse area at the same multiplicity and a larger area gives a softer spectrum. The softening decreases towards peripheral collisions and is the same at forward pseudorapidity. In central collisions the spectral shape follows the centrality class more closely than the multiplicity. The same procedure is tested in Xe+Xe and Pb+Pb collisions.

papers.title: On the effective atmospheric-scale $ m^2$ in neutrino oscillation
papers.abstract: We discuss an effective two-frequency description of the three-generation neutrino oscillation with the key quantity $\Delta m^2_{ \text{effective} }$, which unifies the effects of atmospheric-scale $\Delta m^2_{31}$-$\Delta m^2_{32}$ driven oscillations. As a solution to the minimization problem in vacuum, Nunokawa {\it et al.} obtained $\Delta m^2_{ \text{effective} } = \Delta m^2_{31} - (2E / L) \arctan \left\{ r_{2} \sin 2\Delta_{21} / ( r_{1} + r_{2} \cos 2\Delta_{21} ) \right\}$, where $\Delta_{21} \equiv \Delta m^2_{21} L / (4 E)$ and $r_{i}$ are the mixing-angle dependent constants. Despite the skepticism for the $L/E$ dependence in this formula, we show, in fact, that this is an exact expression, which renders the probability formula also exact. We offer an appealing-to-intuition physical explanation for the $L/E$ dependence that it originates from the nature-designed three generation neutrinos. The way it is buried into $\Delta m^2_{ \text{effective} }$ is through the solar-effect renormalization to this quantity. With the physical interpretation of $\Delta m^2_{ \text{effective} }$ at hand, we aim at resolving the existing controversies on $\Delta m^2_{ \text{effective} }$ in this paper.

papers.title: Area-minimizing surfaces and the rigidity of three-dimensional electrostatic systems
papers.abstract: We study three-dimensional electrostatic systems, the Riemannian data of static solutions of the Einstein--Maxwell equations with cosmological constant $\Lambda$, by means of locally area-minimizing surfaces. Such a surface with non-empty boundary on the horizons is a totally geodesic hemisphere and forces the de Sitter system. A closed one in the interior forces a system of product type, one of eight models if the scalar curvature is somewhere positive on it, among them the Bertotti--Robinson, Nariai and cold and ultracold black hole systems. No compactness, asymptotic or pinching assumption is needed. In particular, closed systems without horizons are flat or compact quotients of the Nariai--Bertotti--Robinson system. For compact systems with connected horizon, the electric field vanishes even when the system is not simply connected, and the area of the horizon is either $12\pi/\Lambda$, for de Sitter, or at most $4\pi/\Lambda$. With several horizons, every horizon whose area does not exceed the sum of the others is stable, minimizes area in its homology class and satisfies an area--charge inequality, with equality only for the charged Nariai systems; its charged Hawking mass and charge therefore lie in the parameter region of the Reissner--Nordstr\"om--de Sitter black holes. Compact systems with horizons are spherical space forms with balls removed. Noncompact systems with strictly mean-convex ends have one end, and their horizons are stable and $\pi_1$-injective and satisfy a strict area--charge inequality.

papers.title: Horizon dynamical entropies and phase space topology
papers.abstract: We study phase space topologies induced by infinite-dimensional norms as a means to solve the problem of 'integrability' of Hamiltonian generators corresponding to diffeomorphisms of a null hypersurface, with the specific goal in mind to compare different prescriptions for the dynamical entropy of black holes, which replaces the area in non-stationary regimes. We first show that for a scalar field, there exists a family of norms that would provide integrability for different polarizations. We then show that a single member of this family applies to the gravitational field, and it is given by the Sobolev norm already considered in the literature. The obstruction to the other candidates lies in the semi-positivity of the metric.

papers.title: Entanglement island and Page curve for one-sided rotating Kerr black holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the information paradox for one-sided asymptotically flat rotating Kerr black holes formed through gravitational collapse using the island prescription. Near the horizon, the dynamics of a scalar field can be described by an effective two-dimensional theory, which provides the framework for our analysis. We study how rotation affects the location of the island boundary $\partial I$, the Page time, and the scrambling time, treating non-extremal and extremal Kerr black holes separately. For non-extremal black holes, the emergence of an island prevents the unbounded growth of Hawking radiation entropy at late times and restores the unitary Page curve. We further find that the island boundary depends on the location of the cutoff surface, in contrast to the behaviour found for eternal Kerr black holes. In the extremal case, the late-time entanglement entropy of Hawking radiation approaches the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of the extremal black hole. Our results demonstrate the important role of black hole geometry in determining the behaviour of entanglement entropy and suggest that the island prescription provides a semiclassical resolution of the information paradox for one-sided rotating Kerr black holes.

papers.title: A homogeneous mass campaign of transiting sub-Neptunes around FGK stars
papers.abstract: Sub-Neptunes are among the most common planets in our Galaxy, but are still poorly understood. Addressing their origins and compositions requires precise bulk densities, but literature values come from studies using different radial velocity (RV) extraction methods, stellar activity treatments, and statistical frameworks, which introduces systematic biases that can lead to spurious conclusions in population-level analyses. We conducted a systematic and homogeneous mass-measurement campaign for 12 sub-Neptune systems observed by Kepler and K2, selected for their absent or poorly constrained masses ($\sigma_{M_p}/M_p > 25\%$). Using new HIRES, HARPS-N, and ESPRESSO spectroscopy as well as archival data, we applied a unified hierarchical Bayesian framework with homogeneous data curation. For HARPS-N and ESPRESSO, we applied four independent extraction pipelines (CCF, SERVAL, LBL, sBART) and combined the posteriors via leave-one-out cross-validation stacking, so that no mass would hinge on a single pipeline. A preferred noise model for each target was selected through a uniform Bayesian procedure. We obtained $>3\sigma$ masses for four transiting planets: Kepler-21 b ($5.66^{+0.65}_{-0.96} M_\oplus$, $7.61^{+0.96}_{-1.28}$ g cm$^{-3}$), K2-66 b ($17.9 \pm 3.2 M_\oplus$, $4.69 \pm 1.31$ g cm$^{-3}$), Kepler-538 b ($10.8^{+2.4}_{-2.8} M_\oplus$), and K2-182 b ($20.1^{+4.5}_{-7.8} M_\oplus$). We also provide updated masses for the non-transiting giants Kepler-65 e and Kepler-129 d, and upper limits for the remaining 15 signals, including the first constraints for K2-184, K2-244, and K2-269. No new non-transiting companion was detected in any system. The semi-amplitudes of the four reductions span a median of $0.75\sigma$ of the stacked posterior, and up to $2.7\sigma$, a systematic that a single-pipeline analysis would ignore.

papers.title: The ALMA REBELS Survey: multi-band dust continuum observations reveal heavily obscured starbursts among UV-bright galaxies at $z7$
papers.abstract: Detailed studies with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) have shown that dust is widespread even in UV-luminous galaxies at $z\gtrsim6.5$. Multi-band continuum observations are critical to fully characterize these early dust reservoirs. We present a homogeneous analysis of multi-band ALMA observations from the REBELS Large Program and seven follow-up programs, targeting thirteen massive galaxies at $6.5\lesssim z\lesssim7.7$ in at least two bands, including Band 8. Through optically thin modified blackbody fitting, we infer the dust masses, temperatures, and infrared luminosities of our targets. Their dust temperatures span $T_\mathrm{dust}\approx30-70\,\mathrm{K}$, and a stack reveals an average $T_\mathrm{dust}=49_{-8}^{+11}\,\mathrm{K}$. Three sources nominally qualify as ultra-luminous infrared galaxies (ULIRGs; $L_\mathrm{IR}>10^{12}\,L_\odot$), with total star formation rates of $\mathrm{SFR}_\mathrm{UV+IR}\approx160-300\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, the highest of which is found in our most distant target, REBELS-18 at $z=7.67$. Their star formation is heavily obscured, with $\gtrsim90\%$ emerging in the infrared, compared to an already large average obscured fraction of $f_\mathrm{obs}=0.75\pm0.11$ for the stack. These SFRs are consistent with the reconstructed growth histories of some massive quiescent galaxies at $z\approx4-5$, suggesting that dusty yet UV-bright galaxies at $z\sim7$ are plausible progenitors of such systems. The sample moreover displays large dust-to-stellar mass ratios ($M_\mathrm{dust}/M_\star = 0.4_{-0.2}^{+0.3}\%$), best reproduced by models in which dust grows efficiently in the interstellar medium. This demonstrates that a dust-rich, IR-luminous, and heavily obscured galaxy population is already in place well into the Epoch of Reionization.

papers.title: Kepler-404: A near-resonant pair of sub-Neptunes. Reinterpreting a false-positive signal with the novel detection method RIVERS.radon
papers.abstract: According to the current understanding of planet formation and evolution, (near)-resonant systems should be a common occurrence in nature. However, pairs of planets with period ratios close to commensurability are rarely observed. In this paper, we discuss how observational bias caused by transit timing variations (TTVs) can affect the detection of low signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) planets in transit surveys, playing a role in the lack of representation of these systems. We present an alternative detection method, RIVERS.radon, which overcomes the effect of TTVs on planet detectability by not relying on an exact periodic solution for the transit signal. It leverages 2D representations of the light curve and approximates the transits with a set of local periodic solutions with the use of 2D cross-correlation. We present an application of RIVERS.radon to the near-resonant system Kepler-404, showing that the signal of the false-positive candidate KOI-2768.03 belongs to the planet Kepler-404b and that it is in a near 5:4 resonance with its companion Kepler-404c, causing TTVs of amplitudes 117.64 and 110.09 minutes, respectively. With a photodynamical fit, we retrieve a pair of similar planets, respectively of radii $1.68^{+0.09}_{-0.09}$ and $1.69^{+0.10}_{-0.10}\,R_\oplus$ and of masses $1.91^{+0.41}_{-0.33}$ and $2.34^{+0.47}_{-0.40}\,M_\oplus$. We find that these planets exhibit typical (near)-resonant features: their densities are lower than the bulk population of exoplanets, and their orbits are nearly coplanar. Interestingly, the planets are found outside the resonance but at a significant distance from the equilibrium point of the $(X_{\rm res}, \delta)$ plane of the Hamiltonian, which is consistent with post-disk instability but somewhat at odds with the observed coplanarity.

papers.title: Photometric Characterisation and Evolutionary State Investigation of the Low Mass-Ratio Contact Binary FASTT 1558
papers.abstract: Contact binaries with low mass ratios, as potential progenitors of stellar mergers, offer important insights into the physical processes governing mass and energy transfer. In this work, we present the first spectro-photometry based evolutionary investigation of FASTT 1558, a totally eclipsing, low mass-ratio contact binary. We combine TESS and ASAS-SN photometry with phase-resolved spectroscopy obtained with the 3.6m Devasthal Optical Telescope. The lightcurve modeling with PHOEBE shows that the system has an exceptionally low secondary-to-primary mass ratio of $q=0.1544\pm0.0013$, with a deep contact degree of $f=0.61\pm0.01$. Our analysis yields a total system mass of $1.92\pm0.31\,M_\odot$, while the distance to the system is estimated to be $648.45\pm29.85$ pc. Analysis of long-term eclipse timings reveals an apparent orbital period decrease of $\dot{P}=-(3.03\pm0.26) \times 10^{-7}$ ${\rm day\,yr^{-1}}$, which may be associated with mass-transfer from the primary to the secondary on a thermal timescale. The spectra show phase-dependent H$\alpha$ and CaII equivalent widths, indicating a dynamically evolving chromosphere. Binary evolution calculations with MESA terminates through L2 overflow before reaching the observed low mass-ratio. Despite its extreme mass ratio, the system is presently Darwin stable, with $J_{\rm spin}/J_{\rm orb}=0.15\pm0.02$. FASTT 1558 therefore provides a robust observational benchmark for evolutionary models of low mass-ratio contact binaries.

papers.title: Plasma Heating by Magnetic Reconnection and Alfven Waves in Collisionless Shocks
papers.abstract: In collisionless shock waves, the ion and electron temperatures generally differ, and the mechanisms governing their energy partitioning remain one of the central unresolved problems in shock physics. Although energy can be exchanged through various plasma waves generated upstream and downstream of the shock, large-amplitude Alfven waves excited by ions reflected at the shock front play a particularly important role in high-Mach-number shocks. In this study, we focus on these large-amplitude Alfven waves and examine not only plasma heating through conventional wave-particle interactions but also preferential ion heating driven by magnetic reconnection within current sheets formed by trains of such waves. Using particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations, we find a correlation between ion heating and X-type magnetic field structures in the downstream region, and we suggest that magnetic reconnection and magnetic annihilation within these current sheets influence the energy partitioning between ions and electrons.

papers.title: Exact Mass Multipoles of Distorted Schwarzschild Spacetimes
papers.abstract: Using the isolated-horizon framework, we compute the geometric and mass multipole moments of the Weyl-distorted Schwarzschild horizon without linearizing the distortion. Starting from the exact integral representation we evaluate it in closed form for two cases, a pure quadrupole distortion and a dipole-quadrupole-octupole distortion. For a pure quadrupole we obtain a closed form for all $\ell$ in terms of confluent hypergeometric functions, while for a dipole-quadrupole-octupole distortion we derive a closed-form series solution in the odd-parity coefficient $\beta$ whose coefficients are exact in the quadrupole coefficient $\alpha_{2}$. We use these results to understand the errors incurred by leading-order approximations. Leading-order approximations in $\alpha_{2}$ misestimate every dimensionless mass multipole by a relative error of roughly $\alpha_{2}$, nearly independent of $\ell$, and for pure linearization most of the error lies in the linearized quadrupole moment rather than the discarded higher multipoles. A simple degree-counting rule determines which orders of distortion contribute to each multipole. As a consequence, the odd-parity component must be small compared with $\alpha_{2}^2$ before it can be neglected. Finally, truncating the series in $\beta$ at its first $\beta$-dependent order reproduces the $\ell \leq 6$ multipoles to about $10^{-3}$ for $|\beta|,|\alpha_{2}| \leq 1/8$.

papers.title: Assessing the total mass of the Planck protocluster candidates with CMB lensing stacking
papers.abstract: Galaxy clusters in formation, or protoclusters, are important sites regarding the evolution of large scale structures and the star formation history of the Universe. With a few exceptions, only their member galaxies have been routinely observed so far. The majority of their mass is expected to be under the form of non baryonic dark matter and cold intergalactic gas. The Planck high redshift star-forming field sample compiles 2151 protocluster candidates, among which 1012 fall within the footprint of the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). The lensing of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) by foreground structures allows us to try and assess the total mass of these protoclusters for the first time. We stack the CMB lensing data from ACT at the location of the Planck protocluster candidates to obtain a mean convergence signal. We then provide an estimate for the mean mass along the line of sight for these objects. The centre of the stacked field corresponds to a lensing signal at a $12\,\sigma$ significance level. The integration of the mass along the line of sight yields a value of $(6.6\pm 1.4) \times 10^{14}\,M_\odot$, similar to what is expected from numerical simulations. With the constraint $1.5 < z < 3$ from Planck, we are able to rule out the possibility that this sample is populated by virialised massive structures. This is the first time that the mass of Planck high redshift sources is measured in such a direct way. The results we obtain constitute a new strong argument in favour of this sample being composed of a majority of galaxy protoclusters lying at $z \geq 1$.

papers.title: The 2026 iron meteorite fall near Zadzim (Poland) and atmospheric ablation of iron meteoroids
papers.abstract: Understanding the process of penetration of cosmic material through the Earth's atmosphere is important for linking the atmospheric and ground effects with the properties of original bodies. It has been shown previously that the main process affecting the fate of stony impactors is atmospheric fragmentation. Much less is known about iron impactors,mainly because the scarcity of data about actual iron meteorite falls. Here we present the trajectory, dynamics, light curve, spectrum, and orbit of a fireball which occurred on April 17, 2026, over Poland and was observed by the European Fireball Network and the Skytinel Network. Based on the fireball observations, single 2.9 kg iron meteorite was recovered in the municipality of Zadzim. Analysis of the fireball data revealed no fragmentation although the body suffered a relatively large dynamic pressure of 5.2 MPa. Fitting the light curve needed luminous efficiency 3 times larger than for stony meteoroids. The initial mass was about 19 kg, corresponding to an effective size of 17 cm. We fitted the light curves of 7 other fireballs produced by iron meteoroids with sizes of 2.5 - 13 cm. The ablation coefficient reached enormously high values of about 1 kg/MJ in small meteoroids causing the material to be exhausted and the fireball to end suddenly high in the atmosphere. In the present case, the value did not exceed 0.08 kg/MJ and relaxed to 0.023 kg/MJ towards the end, enabling part of the meteoroid to survive as meteorite. We conclude that the fate of iron meteoroids strongly depends on their size. The reason probably is the high thermal conductivity of iron which leads to complete overheating and easy melting of smaller meteoroids. The orbits of 44 iron fireballs are also provided.

papers.title: Sulfur chemistry in temperate N$_2$-dominated exoplanetary atmospheres investigated through experimental simulations: Volatile characterization
papers.abstract: Aims. This study addresses through an experimental approach an understudied aspect of sulfur atmospheric chemistry which is the coupled and complex reactivity existing between sulfur, carbon, and nitrogen elements. Experimental simulations have been used to better characterize the volatile products resulting from the coupling between these three elements and discuss the potential observability of such species. Sulfur chemistry appears as a source of diversified signatures which need to be characterized for the current and the future exploration of exoplanetary atmospheres. Methods. SO$_2$ and H$_2$S reactivity was explored experimentally in plasma discharges using mixtures of either pure N$_2$ or composed of N$_2$ and CH$_4$. The volatile species produced in such conditions were analyzed and quantified by in situ mass spectrometry. Results. SO$_2$ reactivity in the presence of N$_2$ alone or combined with methane led to the detection of six sulfur species: H$_2$S, NHSO, S$_2$O, CS$_2$, OCS, and CH$_3$SH. Under the same conditions, the reactivity of H$_2$S resulted in the observation of CS$_2$, CS, and CH$_3$SH. The detection of these species highlights the need to establish a consistent photochemical network describing this sulfur chemistry. Furthermore, the study addresses the detectability of these sulfur compounds via transit spectroscopy. Among them, OCS and CS$_2$, exhibit several detectable bands in the mid-infrared, and constitute promising targets to probe sulfur active chemistry with space- telescopes. In contrast, the detection of the other sulfur volatiles observed appears more challenging at low spectral resolution.

papers.title: The evolution of discs and the epoch of formation of giant planets around low-mass stars
papers.abstract: Large-grain depletion in the inner discs of young stellar systems provides a potential observational signature of dust filtration by forming giant-planet cores. In a previous study, we found that $0.50\pm0.10$ of prominent protoplanetary discs around solar-type stars ($0.7$--$1.5$~\Msun) with ages of 2--8~Myr show evidence for a depletion of large grains inside the snow line. Such a depletion may arise when a sufficiently massive planetary core acts as a barrier to the inward drift of large grains, filtering them from the inner disc. If this interpretation is correct, the frequency of dust-filtration signatures should decrease towards lower stellar masses, in accordance with the lower occurrence rate of giant planets around low-mass stars. Extending our analysis to lower-mass stars, we found that only $0.09\pm0.09$ of discs around stars with masses of $0.30$--$0.58$~\Msun, corresponding to the progenitors of main-sequence early M-type stars, show evidence of grain filtration. This fraction is lower than that measured for solar-type stars and is consistent with the lower frequency of giant planets around M-type stars. We also found that discs exhibiting evidence of filtration tend to have relatively massive outer dust reservoirs, with dust masses exceeding $20$~\MEarth. Conversely, the absence of filtration signatures in lower-mass discs suggests that Neptune-mass and lower-mass planets, despite being common around low-mass stars, may generally be unable to filter large grains efficiently.

papers.title: Robustness of Transition Probabilities of Spectral Lines Deduced from Spatially Resolved Solar Spectra
papers.abstract: Atomic parameters are a key ingredient for the synthesis of spectral lines to model observed spectra and to extract meaningful physical information about the observed astrophysical object. We use quiet-sun observations to test the reliability of the atomic parameter inference from observed spectra. Our focus is on the transition probability of spectral lines, denoted as log(gf). We apply a spectropolarimetric inversion method to quiet-sun disc-centre observations at 1.56 $\mu$m from the GRIS/GREGOR spectrograph. We use the coupled method implemented in the globin inversion code, where atomic parameters are spatially coupled, and a single value of these parameters is determined for every spectral line over the entire field of view. We carry out tests to determine the sensitivity of the inferred log(gf) values to various atmospheric parameters and the data reduction fallibility. We find that our log(gf) values are weaker by 0.023 dex compared to the most recent study. This is most probably caused by the constraint imposed on the log(gf) parameter due to the spatial coupling, lifting the degeneracy between temperature and log(gf). We use the Markov chain Monte Carlo method to determine the uncertainty in the inferred log(gf) values. For the strongest lines in the spectral region, the uncertainty in log(gf) is 1-4 %, increasing to 12 % for weaker and blended lines. Our tests suggest that the log(gf) values inferred using the coupled method from globin are robust against any local contamination to the observed line profiles, such as spectral stray light, and return a reliable and unique set of log(gf) values for the strongest lines irrespective of the chosen atmospheric model and observation dataset. This result is valid as long as the underlying assumptions of line formation under local thermodynamic equilibrium and the completeness of the line list are satisfied.

papers.title: Electron processing of glycine: evidence for peptide-forming condensation reactions
papers.abstract: The discovery of amino acids on asteroids, including samples returned from asteroid Bennu, and the detection of glycine on comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko support the hypothesis that glycine can form in extraterrestrial environments. Laboratory experiments show that glycine can form through both energetic and non-energetic processing of interstellar ice analogues. In the interstellar medium, glycine is exposed to various forms of energetic processing, including cosmic rays and the secondary electrons they generate, which have been shown to produce complex organic molecules, including peptides. This work investigates whether peptide-forming chemistry is a general consequence of energetic processing. Films of glycine and glycine-d3 were grown in two ultrahigh-vacuum chambers and irradiated with 1-2 keV electrons. The irradiated samples were subsequently characterised using infrared spectroscopy, temperature-programmed desorption, and vacuum-ultraviolet spectroscopy. Peptide formation through condensation reactions would produce water as a secondary product, and spectra obtained following irradiation of glycine-d3 showed evidence of D2O formation, supported by TPD measurements, which revealed H2O formation for glycine and H2O, HDO, and D2O for glycine-d3. VUV spectra of irradiated glycine showed the formation of decomposition products, including CO and CO2, as well as H2O. Following heating, a non-volatile residue remained on the surface. Electron irradiation of glycine produces reaction products similar to proton irradiation, suggesting that the resulting chemistry is not strongly dependent on the energy source. These findings support the possibility that larger organic molecules can form in a wide range of extraterrestrial environments. Such molecules may subsequently be incorporated into small bodies and delivered to planetary surfaces, potentially contributing to the emergence of life.

papers.title: Robust Measurements of the Cosmic Microwave Background Lensing Power Spectrum in the Presence of Anisotropic Cosmic Birefringence
papers.abstract: Achieving the scientific potential of upcoming high-sensitivity cosmic microwave background (CMB) polarization surveys requires lensing analyses that are robust to unmodeled distortions of the polarization field. One such possible distortion is anisotropic cosmic birefringence, a direction-dependent rotation of the linear polarization plane that may arise from parity-violating physics such as axion-like fields. We quantify the impact of both modeled and unmodeled anisotropic birefringence on the CMB lensing measurement in the Marginal Unbiased Score Expansion (MUSE) framework. Considering noise levels expected for current and future CMB surveys, we find that neglecting birefringence produces a positive bias in the lensing bandpowers that increases towards small angular scales. For a scale-invariant birefringence power spectrum $L(L+1)C_L^{\alpha\alpha}/2\pi=10^{-5}\,{\rm rad}^2$, the positive fractional bias can reach $(10.1\pm1.1)\%$ of the lensing power at $1375<2000$. Jointly estimating lensing and birefringence in the MUSE framework recovers the input lensing bandpowers and birefringence amplitude without detectable bias across all tested configurations. The joint MUSE estimator also reduces the scatter of the recovered birefringence amplitude by factors of $1.6\pm0.2$ to $2.4\pm0.3$ relative to a joint quadratic estimator, with the largest gains in the highest signal-to-noise configurations. These results indicate that a joint-field reconstruction with MUSE can recover unbiased estimates of the lensing and birefringence power spectra while still improving precision relative to quadratic estimators.

papers.title: Nonlinear models of Mira variables with long secondary periods
papers.abstract: Calculations of nonlinear radial oscillations in asymptotic giant branch stars with an initial mass of $M_\mathrm{ZAMS}=1.6M_\odot$ were performed for initial helium and metal abundances of $Y=0.28$ and $Z=0.006$, respectively. Several models from the evolutionary sequence after the 4th thermal pulse were used as initial conditions for the hydrodynamic equations describing stellar pulsations with long secondary periods. Using the discrete Fourier transform of the hydrodynamic solutions we show that long secondary periods appear in Mira variables pulsating simultaneously in the fundamental mode and first overtone with non-multiple periods. The relative deviation from multiplicity is $\delta_\mathrm{\Pi}\le 1.2\times 10^{-2}$ and is responsible for mode splitting into equally spaced frequency components, each of which is a standing wave with a free outer boundary. The cycle length of long secondary periods is nearly 20 times that of the fundamental mode. Long secondary periodicity is a nonlinear effect that arises after reaching the limiting amplitude and develops over several hundred fundamental mode periods.

papers.title: Jupiter's Evolving Interior as a Source of Episodic Heating on Europa
papers.abstract: Jupiter's evolving interior can affect the orbital evolution of its moons through frequency-dependent tidal dissipation. We investigate how encounters between the Galilean satellites and Jupiter's oscillation modes affect the stability of the Laplace resonance and Europa's tidal heating. Using the N-body integrator REBOUNDx, we simulate the dynamical orbital evolution of Io, Europa, and Ganymede, with tidal migration timescales derived from three representative models of Jupiter's interior. Encounters with a Jovian tidal resonance can alter the libration state of the Laplace angle, excite orbital eccentricity, and/or destroy the Laplace resonant chain. The outcome of the satellite system depends on which moon experiences enhanced tidal migration. Resonance locks involving Io or Europa can sustain outward migration of the Laplace resonant chain, whereas Ganymede locks destroy the chain. Notably, transient resonance crossings can excite Europa's eccentricity without breaking the Laplace resonance. Under our adopted eccentricity-damping prescription, the baseline tidal power is typically of the order $10^{11}$-$10^{12}$ W, with transient episodes reaching roughly an order of magnitude higher power. These results provide a mechanism for episodic tidal heating on Europa without requiring thermal feedback within the satellites.

papers.title: Thermal evolution of Uranus and Neptune, hydrogen-water phase separation and the role of methane
papers.abstract: Adiabatic evolution models of Uranus and Neptune with constant compositional stratification miss their observed luminosities: Uranus is fainter than commonly predicted, while improved equations of state (EoS) have recently led to a brightness problem for Neptune. In adiabatic models of Jupiter and Saturn, helium rain is thought to enhance luminosity. In the ice giants, hydrogen-water phase separation (H2-H2O demixing) with water rain has recently been predicted. We aim to understand how H2-H2O demixing and the EoS of water influence the luminosity of Uranus and Neptune. We use state-of-the-art EoS of H, He, H2O, and the H2-H2O phase diagram to build adiabatic three-layer models of the present-day structure that match the observed gravity field and the phase diagram. We compute evolution tracks with and without demixing, and for Neptune, with and without latent heat and methane, for which we provide an updated large-scale EoS including entropy. Without demixing, adiabatic Neptune with the revised AQUA EoS, without methane or latent heat, cools to its observed luminosity within 4.5 Gyr, in good agreement with the age of the Solar system. Applying the same assumptions to Uranus would require a Bond albedo of 0.43 to explain its luminosity. With demixing, the radii expand while the luminosity decreases. For Uranus, demixing leads to an equilibrium evolution with the incident flux that naturally explains its faintness. Demixing also makes Neptune fainter. Methane reduces the radius expansion but not the faintness problem. Favored Neptune models include demixing and methane at an initial C/O ratio of $\sim$1 due to CO ice accretion, with cooling times of $\lesssim 4 Gyr. Neptune requires an additional heat source unless its structure is primordial and the outer envelope is ice-poor, while hydrogen-water phase separation is an option to explain the structure and faintness of Uranus.

papers.title: Machine learning enables full Bayesian inference for spinning extreme-mass-ratio inspirals
papers.abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs), stellar-mass compact objects spiralling into massive black holes, promise to measure the masses and spins of the central black holes, reveal the strong-field environment around them and gauge cosmic distances via millihertz gravitational-wave observations. Yet most forecasts for the parameter inference of these systems assume known source parameters, and broad-prior analyses have addressed only simplified versions of the problem. The joint inversion of all 14 parameters of a spinning source from the complete prior has remained unsolved. Here we solve it for the augmented analytic kludge model: generative networks narrow the complete prior and reveal a ring of degenerate spin directions, and the exact detector likelihood determines the posterior. For a simulated one-year LISA-Taiji observation, within one ring sector we obtain, for the first time, a 14-parameter posterior of a spinning EMRI from the complete prior, the most precise yet obtained for such a source from broad priors. The redshifted mass and spin of the massive black hole are determined to two parts in $10^5$, the mass two orders of magnitude beyond any electromagnetic measurement. The compact object's redshifted mass is measured to one part in $10^4$, and its eccentric, retrograde orbit discriminates between capture channels. The 0.8% distance and sub-square-degree localization are sufficient for dark-siren cosmology. Year-long coherent analysis resolves the inspiral driven by radiation reaction itself.

papers.title: Classical phase space distributions for quantum states in cosmology: General states, operator ordering and the geometry of fading non-commutativity
papers.abstract: In earlier work with Ashtekar and Kesavan we showed that, for linear fields in any FLRW background, the vacuum defines a probability distribution $\rho_o$ on the classical phase space whose moments are exactly the Weyl-ordered $n$-point functions. We extend that analysis in four directions. First, for an arbitrary state $\Psi$ we give an explicit formula, in the Bargmann representation, for the distribution $\rho_\Psi$ that reproduces all Weyl-ordered expectation values. For pure states it is non-negative precisely for coherent and squeezed states, each the Gaussian of a compatible K\"ahler metric, and the Gaussian smoothing needed to make it positive is either zero or the full coherent-state width. Second, for linear observables every operator ordering differs from the Weyl ordering by explicit products of $c$-number commutators. Third, for two linear observables in a pure Gaussian state, the classical correlation coefficient, the ratio of commutator to anticommutator and the squeezing are functions of a single angle between their Hamiltonian vector fields; this bounds the departure of arbitrarily ordered $n$-point functions from the moments of $\rho$. Fourth, for fields in FLRW the equality holds at arbitrary, possibly different, times and for every homogeneous isotropic quasi-free state. In de Sitter the non-commutative corrections fall as $e^{-N}$ for field and momentum and as $e^{-3N}/3$ for the field at two times. For the state inherited from inflation they stay suppressed in the radiation era, by the inverse occupation number, except near the nodes of the mode functions. The same squeezing entangles the modes $\pm\vec k$ relative to the radiation-era vacuum and makes displaced-parity measurements violate Bell inequalities, so the positive distribution describes a specified family of observables, not all measurements.

papers.title: Tentative Excess Dispersion Measures toward DESI Galaxy Groups from Localized Fast Radio Bursts
papers.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) provide sensitive probes of ionized baryons through their dispersion measures (DMs). In this work, we test whether localized FRB sight lines intersecting foreground galaxy groups exhibit a measurable excess in cosmic DM relative to clean nonintersecting sight lines. We crossmatch 117 localized FRBs with measured DMs and host redshifts against a foreground group catalog from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. Within the catalog footprint and at $z_{\rm host}<0.5$, we identify 23 sight lines intersecting foreground groups and 18 clean nonintersecting sight lines for the main comparison. A joint fit to this sample gives a positive offset of $143.3^{+53.2}_{-53.0}~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ in the inferred cosmic DM, $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm cosmic}$, for the group-intersecting sight lines relative to the nonintersecting control sample. A template fit for the foreground halos gives $A_{\rm halo}=0.34^{+0.51}_{-0.50}$, with a positive posterior median but a weakly constrained detailed halo contribution. A mock forecast within the DESI footprint indicates that larger samples of localized FRBs would improve the foreground halo template constraint.

papers.title: H$_3^+$ forbidden rotational lines in a planetary nebula: JWST/MIRI detection in the Ring Nebula and ionization by the central star
papers.abstract: We report the detection of the forbidden pure rotational spectrum of H$_3^+$ in the Ring Nebula (NGC 6720), to our knowledge the first detection of H$_3^+$ in a planetary nebula. In JWST/MIRI spectra obtained toward the inner edge of the main ring, 0.1 pc in projection from the central star, the $(J,K) = (5,0)\to(4,3)$ line at 16.325 $\mu$m is detected at $32\sigma$, along with nine further unblended lines. The H$_3^+$ emission spatially follows the H$_2$ emission, whose rotational lines show warm (660 K) and hot (1700 K) components. A statistical-equilibrium model at these temperatures reproduces the subthermal H$_3^+$ line pattern, with much of the emission arising in the hot H$_2$. The emission requires an H$_2$ ionization rate of $\sim 3\times 10^{-12}\,{\rm s^{-1}}$ in the hot H$_2$ for an electron fraction of $2\times 10^{-4}$. The rate is $\sim 2\times 10^4$ times the cosmic-ray ionization rate in diffuse clouds. The extreme-ultraviolet and soft X-ray radiation (54-300 eV) of the 135 kK central star supplies this rate if the hot H$_2$ lies within an H-nucleus column density of (4-8)$\times 10^{19}\,{\rm cm^{-2}}$ of the ionization front of the dense globules. Static photoionization models, however, place the H$_2$ in gas too cold to excite the H$_3^+$ lines. The warm molecular gas and its H$_3^+$ thus suggest dynamical effects, most plausibly the advection of H$_2$ through a photoevaporation front into gas heated by the star. H$_3^+$ provides a new probe of the photoionization of molecular gas by very hot stars.

papers.title: Learning to find cosmic filaments with graph neural networks
papers.abstract: Inferring the large-scale structure of the Universe from galaxy surveys is a fundamental challenge in cosmology. In particular, cosmic filaments form an extended and geometrically complex network whose underlying structure cannot be reconstructed from discrete galaxy catalogs without uncertainty. We investigate a generative approach to filament finding based on flow matching and graph neural networks. The learned model reproduces key statistical properties of the target filament distribution while generating a distribution over possible filament configurations, demonstrating its ability to model uncertainty. Our work provides a first step towards probabilistic inference of the cosmic web directly from galaxy surveys. More broadly, these results demonstrate the potential of conditional generative models for reconstructing filament-like structures from sparse observational tracers.

papers.title: Anisotropic Fluid Inhomogeneous Cosmology
papers.abstract: We propose a new framework for inhomogeneous cosmology based on General Relativity sourced by an anisotropic fluid. The model is parametrized by a single input function, the radial Misner--Sharp mass distribution at different redshifts, and admits exact solutions to Einstein's equations. Going beyond the standard assumption of small metric perturbations, it provides a fully relativistic framework to describe the non-linear regime of cosmic structure formation. The Friedmann-Lema\^itre-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) cosmology is recovered both at early times and -- on large scales only -- at late times. Our Anisotropic Fluid Inhomogeneous Cosmology (AFIC) model provides a natural mechanism through which matter inhomogeneities give rise to late-time acceleration. The extensive term driving this effect does not enter the exact metric solution and therefore does not contribute to the local gravitational potential. Rather, it emerges as a genuinely large-scale effect induced by the inhomogeneous distribution of matter at late times. This mechanism may provide a physical interpretation of the results from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). Finally, we present a simple analytical realization of the model and use it to provide an estimate of the present-day effective dark energy density.

papers.title: Symbolic Regression Diagnostics of 1D Lyman Alpha Forest Emulator
papers.abstract: We use symbolic regression to diagnose the parameter dependence of a black-box multi-fidelity emulator of the Lyman-alpha forest 1D flux power spectrum. Symbolic regression is appealing in its ability to reduce complex parameter spaces, thereby reducing compute time and offering potential interpretability in parameter inter-dependencies. Starting from a pretrained Gaussian-process (GP) emulator that connects low- and high-resolution PRIYA simulations, we search for explicit equations describing the dependence of the power spectrum on resolution and each cosmological and astrophysical parameter. We find that symbolic regression can recover equations that reproduce the emulator values well, but accurate predictions do not guarantee accurate parameter derivatives, making such equations unreliable for downstream applications such as Fisher forecasts. We therefore introduce a derivative-faithfulness diagnostic that directly compares the parameter gradient of each symbolic equation to the GP, and explore a derivative-matching (Sobolev) loss to improve this agreement. At z = 3.6, the Sobolev objective yields derivative-faithful equations for 9 of the 11 PRIYA parameters constraining the Lyman-alpha forest, with the approach only ineffective on h and AGN, whose 1D power spectrum imprints are weak or degenerate. Redefining the training objective with the Sobolev loss is a more robust and computationally efficient approach to gradient-matching repair than increasing model complexity. Our methods present potential mitigation strategies for failure modes of PySR, enabling downstream Fisher forecasts in some of these cases. Further, we document limitations potentially relevant to future work bridging symbolic regression with emulators. Our results demonstrate symbolic regression as an emulator diagnostic tool, with particular utility for low-dimensional or weakly coupled parameter dependencies.

papers.title: Split Ends: UV Physics branches Black Hole Hair
papers.abstract: Coupling a shift-symmetric scalar field to the Gauss-Bonnet invariant modifies black holes (BHs) via scalar hair. Here we consider this field to be the Goldstone of a complex scalar field with a symmetry-breaking potential. For BHs of a size comparable with the inverse mass gap, the gapped field tries to restore the symmetry close to the horizon, enhancing the departure from standard BHs. Moreover, BHs of the same mass can have up to three different horizon areas and surface gravities. This branching has profound consequences for BH physics, potentially observable in gravitational waves.

papers.title: Parallel and perpendicular: a two-population test with POSSUM radio galaxies confirms hint of CMB birefringence
papers.abstract: Analyses of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) polarisation find an isotropic rotation of the linear polarisation plane, cosmic birefringence, of $\beta\sim0.2^\circ$--$0.3^\circ$, hinting at parity-violating physics. An independent test at low redshift with different systematics is needed. Radio galaxies provide such a test because their Faraday de-rotated polarisation angle $\chi_0$ is statistically aligned with their position angle $\psi$. Previous tests fitted only the population with $\chi_0-\psi\approx90^\circ$. We add the population with $\chi_0-\psi\approx0^\circ$, which is rotated by the same angle. We fit $\chi_0-\psi$ with two axial von-Mises distributions plus a uniform background, with an unbinned likelihood including each source's angle error. We apply this to 33,298 components of 16,649 double radio sources from the Polarisation Sky Survey of the Universe's Magnetism (POSSUM), with both components at polarised S/N $>10$ and separated by more than half the beam. Both populations are equally abundant. In the CMB convention we measure $\beta=0.48^\circ\pm0.35^\circ$, agreeing with the CMB in sign and amplitude. Including the $0^\circ$ population halves the variance of $\beta$. Components closer than half a beam carry no information on the source axis; excluding them leaves $\beta$ unchanged and makes the two populations consistent in all morphological classes. Combining with the joint ACT and Planck likelihood for a late-time rotation yields $\beta=0.282^\circ\pm0.056^\circ$, $5.0\sigma$ from zero. At $z\sim0.5$, radio galaxies probe the rotation of the last $\sim$ 5 Gyr. A CMB-sized rotation there would point to a late-evolving field such as axion-like dark energy, whereas a rotation before reionisation, e.g. by axion-like dark matter, predicts $\beta\approx0$. Given absolute angle calibration, the full POSSUM survey can test the CMB result independently.

papers.title: OmniX: A first jet and event model
papers.abstract: Foundation models are a new approach to building machine learning algorithms for particle physics. Their central idea is that a single model can be adapted to a variety of downstream tasks, amortizing training costs. So far, most foundation model prototypes have operated on the constituents of a single jet. This limits their usefulness for physics problems at the scale of full events, such as distinguishing different processes, and restricts their performance, as global correla- tions are invisible to the model. Here, we introduce OmniX, an architecture that operates on both single jets and whole events within a single model. Using the jet-level JetClass and Top-tagging datasets and the event-level Collide-2V dataset, we demonstrate that OmniX trained jointly on single jets and full events matches or exceeds otherwise equivalent jet-only and event-only models in generation and classification.

papers.title: On the evidence of lensing in GW231123
papers.abstract: Just like light, gravitational waves may be gravitationally lensed by massive objects along their travel path, however, this has not been observed so far. GW231123 is the most massive binary black-hole merger observed to-date, and quasi-circular gravitational wave analyses infer high masses and spin parameters that are particularly sensitive to the waveform model used. Here we investigate whether gravitational lensing can account for these features. We model the signal as a superposition of multiple overlapping images of the same merger and find support for lensing across four waveform models. The lensing interpretation reduces the support for these high spins, bringing both the inferred spins and masses into closer agreement across waveform models. A comparison with a background of unlensed signals gives the lensing interpretation an estimated significance of $3.96^{+0.68}_{-0.30}\sigma$. This makes lensing a compelling interpretation of this event but is insufficient for a definitive claim.

papers.title: Probing the X-Ray Structure of the $z = 2.38$ Strongly Lensed Quasar J1721+8842, the First Einstein Zig-Zag Lens, Down to $140 pc$
papers.abstract: Sub-kiloparsec X-ray structures in active galactic nuclei (AGN), including outflows, jets, and dual AGN, provide key insights into their evolution and influence on host galaxies. In the local universe, Chandra X-ray Observatory's state-of-the-art $0.5''$ angular resolution has resolved these structures, but at $z > 0.1$, milliarcsecond resolution is required to spatially resolve sub-kpc scales. We leverage the spatial amplification by strong gravitational lensing to investigate the X-ray structure of J1721+8842, a $z=2.38$ quasar lensed into six images. To reconstruct the optical emission position, we model the lensing mass distribution using the six quasar images, five detected by Gaia Data Release 3 (A-E) and one by HST (F). Our model reproduces the five Gaia image positions to milliarcsecond precision. To locate the X-ray emission relative to the optical, we combine ray-trace simulations of archival Chandra observations with the lens model image position predictions using a double maximum-likelihood analysis. We constrain the X-ray centroid within a $0.017''\times0.004''\ (139\times30\ \mathrm{pc})$ ellipse centered $0.005''\ (44\ \mathrm{pc})$ away from the optical source position. Source-plane reconstructions of the soft-X-ray and hard-X-ray to optical sources demonstrate these emission regions are cospatial, allowing the optical source at $1\sigma$ confidence. These results indicate no evidence for kpc-scale X-ray jets, outflows, or dual AGN with projected separations exceeding $140\ \mathrm{pc}$. This method improves Chandra's effective angular resolution by a factor of 30 at cosmological distances, enabling studies of sub-kpc AGN X-ray structure at cosmic noon.

papers.title: Euclid: Discovery of a quasar at z = 8.13 hosting a 360-million-solar-mass black hole
papers.abstract: Quasars powered by rapid accretion onto supermassive black holes (SMBHs) have been uncovered deep into the first gigayear of cosmic history. We present the discovery of EUCL J150452.291+625224.39 (J1504+6252), selected from Euclid Wide Survey imaging and spectroscopically confirmed as the first quasar at z > 8 through observations with Keck, HST, LBT, and JWST. J1504+6252 exhibits the defining spectral signatures of archetypal quasars at lower redshift, including a luminous blue power-law continuum and broad permitted emission lines, indicating a classical broad-line region. JWST/NIRSpec G395M spectroscopy yields a systemic redshift of z = 8.129 +/- 0.005, corresponding to 630 Myr after the Big Bang and shifting the quasar redshift frontier by about 39 Myr (6% of the age of the Universe at that epoch). From H-beta and Mg II, we measured intrinsic broad-line-region FWHM of 3160 +/- 270 and 3740 (+160/-170) km/s, respectively. A widely used single-epoch H-beta calibration gives a reference black hole mass of log10(MBH/Msun) = 8.56 +/- 0.43. Applying a range of calibrations to both Mg II and H-beta yields log10(MBH/Msun) = 8.33-8.89 and Eddington ratios of 0.12-0.44. Assembling a black hole of several hundred million solar masses within the first few hundred million years, despite its currently sub-Eddington accretion rate, requires either a massive seed or sustained, highly efficient early growth. The discovery of a mature, sub-Eddington quasar at z > 8 suggests that substantially more luminous quasars hosting similarly massive black holes may remain to be discovered. Conversely, previously known reionisation-era quasars may represent the rapidly accreting end of a broader population of already massive black holes spanning a wider range of accretion states.

papers.title: Free hyperboloidal evolution in 3D: gauge waves and constraint-violating gravitational waves
papers.abstract: Hyperboloidal evolution allows to reach future null infinity within numerical relativity simulations. This work extends the conformal compactification approach with BSSN/Z4 from spherical symmetry to full 3D simulations. This is the first free numerical hyperboloidal evolution in 3D with a common formulation of general relativity. In this first step, gauge waves and constraint-violating gravitational waves perturbing Minkowski spacetime are evolved nonlinearly and show that the implementation is reliable and signals can be successfully extracted at future null infinity.

papers.title: Late-time cosmic acceleration from matter inhomogeneities: constraints from DESI DR2 and SNe Ia
papers.abstract: We present the first observational constraints on the Misner-Sharp (MS) mass of the universe, within a newly proposed exact General Relativity solution providing a non-perturbative description of nonlinear cosmic structure formation. At early times, when statistical homogeneity and isotropy are satisfied, our model reduces to usual FLRW cosmology, accommodating Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data. At late times, the departure from homogeneity and isotropy on scales $\lesssim 200$ Mpc -- codified in the scale-dependent redshift distribution of the MS mass -- naturally induces cosmic acceleration, through an extensive term generated by the MS mass asymptotic limit on large scales. We derive the MS mass from Baryon Acoustic Oscillation data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) and Type Ia Supernovae, obtaining a value of the cosmological constant in agreement with $\Lambda$CDM results. We outline broader implications and future observational prospects, highlighting how multi-probe strategies -- particularly CMB lensing and the late Integrated Sachs-Wolfe effect -- can ultimately test this solution to the dark energy puzzle.

papers.title: Discovering Warped Extra Dimensions at Next Generation Dark Matter Detectors
papers.abstract: The coming years will see what could be the final push in the search for WIMP dark matter (DM), with direct detection reaching into the neutrino fog and indirect detection reaching TeV-scale thermal relics. We study a class of models that these experiments could discover: DM emerging from a warped extra dimension. In the IR, these scenarios appear generically as a $Z'$-type portal. We show that DM with electroweak couplings and TeV scale masses remains viable and discoverable within such a bottom-up context. However, the models require a 20\% tuning between the DM and $Z'$ masses, a tuning that is relaxed if the DM and $Z'$ are strongly coupled and heavier ($\sim$$10$ TeV). In fact, it is the strongly-coupled $Z'$-type portal which is UV-completed by the framework of a warped extra-dimensional Grand Unified Theory (GUT), where DM stability is a spin-off of suppressing proton decay, resulting in a $\sim$$10$ TeV Kaluza-Klein (KK) scale. We identify a variant of this framework where all gauge fields except a baryon-number gauge boson have suppressed couplings to the DM; this model significantly suppresses the direct detection rate, but it remains discoverable through indirect detection. Further, to address the little hierarchy problem associated with $\sim$$10$ TeV KK scale, inspired by the Super-Composite Higgs, we augment our extra-dimensional GUT setup with supersymmetry. We show that this model also possesses a DM candidate, now with a weakly-coupled and $\sim$${\rm TeV}$ mass $Z'$ mediator. In all cases, a near-term discovery remains possible, for instance with the now online Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO), suggesting that our first hint of extra dimensions could emerge from the high-energy sky.

papers.title: Enhanced spatial resolution and performance for N-body simulation of self-interacting dark matter
papers.abstract: Studying the implications of self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) on astrophysical objects often requires simulations. N-body simulations are a standard tool but face a few challenges. One is resolving the mean free path in gravothermally collapsing halos. This is necessary to obtain accurate results and is achieved in state-of-the-art simulations by increasing the number of resolution elements. I aim to formulate a numerical scheme that gives an enhanced spatial resolution compared to those methods and allows increasing the resolution without changing the number of resolution elements. The novel scheme that I present is formulated by discarding the classic approach of using kernel functions and computing interaction probabilities. Instead, pairs of particles always interact if their distance is below a specific threshold. Importantly, this distance threshold depends on their relative velocity and the size of the time step. This new formulation no longer requires some of the computations in state-of-the-art schemes and thus helps to increase the performance. Through a variety of test problems with known solutions, I study the accuracy of the new scheme and demonstrate its advantages over state-of-the-art SIDM formulations. Notably, the scheme reduced the computational costs, making the SIDM computations typically much cheaper than gravity. As a consequence, a typical SIDM simulation of isotropic scattering requires only a few percent of its total computational cost for the self-interactions. In conclusion, the new scheme presents an improvement over previous schemes and helps to address current challenges. Besides the enhanced performance, it allows us to achieve a higher accuracy when simulating gravothermally collapsing SIDM halos.

papers.title: JWST/NIRSpec observations of AMORE6 suggest active Pop~III star formation in a self-polluted galaxy
papers.abstract: AMORE6 is a strongly lensed ($\mu\simeq78$), intrinsically faint galaxy at $z=5.725$, previously proposed as a metal-free candidate from the absence of [OIII]$\lambda$5007 in NIRCam slitless spectroscopy. We present deep JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy of its brighter image, AMORE6-B. We detect HeII$\lambda\lambda$1640,4686, with HeII$\lambda$4686/H$\beta=0.080\pm0.015$ and EW(HeII$\lambda$4686)$=35\pm8$ {\AA}, weak [OIII] ($R_3=0.25$) and CIV$\lambda\lambda$1548,51, and no other metal lines. H and He lines give negligible attenuation, $T_e\simeq2\times10^4$ K, and $Y=0.226^{+0.022}_{-0.024}$. The oxygen abundance, $12+\log(O/H)\simeq6.08^{+0.24}_{-0.80}$ (0.04-0.4% $Z_\odot$, depending on the calibration), is the lowest at its stellar mass, while C/O is near or above solar. Photoionization models of different ionizing sources favour metal-free stars with a top-heavy initial mass function (IMF), as in the self-polluted phase of simulated Population III (Pop III) galaxies, or a metal-poor population with a luminous hard X-ray source; ordinary metal-poor populations, very massive stars, and accretion-based sources are disfavoured. A full SED fit in the fiducial self-polluted scenario gives $1.3\times10^5\,M_\odot$ of Pop III stars formed within the last 4 Myr, which ionize mildly enriched gas and leak 86% of their ionizing photons. The HeII-to-Balmer ratio constrains the slope $x$ and characteristic mass $M_{ch}$ of the Pop III IMF jointly, to $90x-268\lesssim M_{ch}/M_\odot\lesssim172x-330$ ($3\sigma$; $M_{ch}\lesssim70\,M_\odot$ for a Salpeter slope), excluding the most top-heavy IMFs allowed by near-field constraints. X-ray binaries are a possible alternative, but require either a metal-poor population too young (1 Myr) to host compact objects and an X-ray luminosity far above that of metal-poor galaxies, or $2\times10^6\,M_\odot$ of older Pop III.2 stars whose metals were mostly expelled.

papers.title: Spectroscopic identification of z>7 quasars with Roman Space Telescope
papers.abstract: The Roman Wide Field Instrument grism will cover a large area over 1.0-1.93 micrometers, making it possible to search directly for Lyman-alpha breaks in quasars beyond redshift z = 7. We simulate quasars at z = 7.5-10 under HLWAS-like exposures with ESpRESSO, including PSF convolution, slitless dispersion, source and background Poisson noise, read noise, and Horne optimal extraction. Three Lyman-alpha equivalent-width (EW) prescriptions are used to bracket the uncertainty in line strength, and the extracted spectra are compared with M/L/T dwarfs and passive red galaxies using the spectral angle mapper. The Lyman-alpha-break completeness remains above 90% to J_AB approximately 23.7-24.1 and reaches 50% at J_AB approximately 24.3-24.7. Beyond J_AB approximately 25, the result depends strongly on the adopted EW distribution. In the fixed-redshift SAM test, the QSO recovery rate is TPR >= 0.982. None of the noisy brown-dwarf or red-galaxy test spectra is classified as a QSO. Because those test spectra are generated from the same finite parent libraries as the reference classes, this result measures the stability of the classification against noise within those libraries rather than an independently calibrated survey false-positive rate. At the faint end, the strongest astrophysical sensitivity in the present calculation is to the high-EW tail of the Lyman-alpha distribution.

papers.title: CosmoMap: Predicting Hot Gas Temperature and Density from Dark Matter with a Conditioned 3D U-Net
papers.abstract: Mock X-ray observations of hot gas in galaxy groups, clusters and the cosmic web require its temperature and density over large volumes and many cosmologies, for which hydrodynamical simulations are expensive. We present CosmoMap, a 3D U-Net FiLM-conditioned on cosmological and feedback parameters that predicts gas temperature $T$ and electron density $n_{\rm e}$ from dark matter density and velocity. On the CAMELS IllustrisTNG Latin hypercube, CosmoMap reaches $R^2 = 0.765$ for $\log T$ and $0.934$ for $\log n_{\rm e}$ at $z=0$, reducing the error of gradient-boosted trees by 22-23 per cent. Temperature is predicted best in the densest regions, mostly galaxy- and group-scale haloes ($R^2 = 0.88$), but the electron density of the brightest X-ray-emitting gas is biased low by $0.12$ dex. One model outperforms the baselines at every redshift up to $z=2$, and using inputs from gravity-only simulations costs little accuracy. The predictions reproduce scaling relations, surface brightness profile shapes and most of the cosmological information in the gas. They produce box-integrated luminosities with a median bias of $-0.16$ dex, sensitive at the $0.2$ dex level to the inference scheme unless batch normalisation is used. Training for per-voxel uncertainties with a heteroscedastic likelihood costs accuracy and lowers luminosities by a further $0.1$-$0.3$ dex; the composite-loss variant, CosmoMap-$\sigma$, provides uncertainties that are calibrated at 68 per cent after rescaling by predicted emissivity, except for the density of the brightest gas. Compact structures are smoothed: mock X-ray lightcones recover 89 per cent of the brightest tenth of sources but 28 per cent of all sources.

papers.title: Magnetar driven Dainotti relation with up to 56% reduced uncertainties: probing the Expansion History of the Universe
papers.abstract: The persistent tension in Hubble constant measurements and recent DESI hints of dynamical dark energy motivate extending the distance ladder beyond Type~Ia supernovae (SNe~Ia) and Cosmic Chronometers (CC) into the largely unexplored range $z\sim2$--$6$. We use X-ray plateau emission of long gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), standardized through the two-dimensional Dainotti relation, as a probe of this gap. We analyze two samples: a platinum sample (P50, 50~GRBs, light-curve quality cuts) and a magnetar sample (M23, 23~GRBs, selected by requiring the magnetar spin-down model to be statistically preferred over the Willingale parametrization). We calibrate the Dainotti relation anchored independently to the Master SNe~Ia compilation and to Cosmic Chronometers, and propagate the result into a joint flat-$\Lambda$CDM inference via MCMC. Despite containing less than half the GRBs of P50, M23 yields an intrinsic scatter $\sim41\%$ smaller, demonstrating that physically motivated selection outperforms quality cuts. Both samples give nearly identical cosmological constraints once combined with SNe~Ia and CC: M23 gives $H_0=69.45\pm0.32\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and $\Omega_m=0.34^{+0.01}_{-0.02}$; P50 gives $H_0=69.46\pm0.33$ and $\Omega_m=0.34\pm0.02$, both in $3$--$3.5\sigma$ tension with Planck and SH0ES. We further introduce a novel joint likelihood that simultaneously fits individual plateau light curves and the Dainotti correlation, reducing the intrinsic scatter by $\sim56\%$ relative to the platinum sample and avoiding local maxima from sparse light-curve data. These results establish magnetar-selected GRB plateaus as a robust, high-redshift complement to existing distance-ladder probes, with a clear path toward improved constraining efficiency as sample sizes grow.

papers.title: $$asmaNet: A Staged Spectral Token-Refinement Architecture for Fast Gravitational-Wave Signal-to-Noise Ratio Prediction
papers.abstract: Quantifying selection effects in gravitational-wave population studies requires millions of costly signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) calculations. We present $\Phi$asmaNet, a compact neural architecture for structured tabular regression, with staged spectral refinement as an explicit architectural prior. Learned input tokens are refined through ordered attention-based $\Phi$-Stages, each augmented by a $\Phi$-Refractor subspace-mixing module, then revisited through gated top-down $\Phi$-Feedback. Applied to the 11-dimensional parameters of precessing, higher-mode binary black hole signals (IMRPhenomXPHM), it predicts phase-averaged optimal SNR for a single detector at fixed Advanced LIGO design sensitivity. With approximately 732k parameters, it outperforms MLP, 1D-ResNet and Transformer-encoder baselines under matched training across $10^5$--$10^6$ samples. At $10^6$ samples, it achieves $100-\mathrm{MAPE}=98.73\%$ on the held-out test set, $99.29\%$ after rank-preserving monotonic (PCHIP) calibration, and $99.39\%$ ($R^2=0.9998$) in the detection-relevant regime $\rho>8$, with stable accuracy across independent dataset realizations. On a single GPU, it sustains approximately $1.2\times10^5$ SNR evaluations per second and processes a $10^6$-injection catalogue end-to-end in approximately 8.3 s, about two orders of magnitude faster than conventional waveform-and-inner-product calculations on a 16-core CPU. Exact distance rescaling through $\rho\propto1/d_L$ supports repeated catalogue-wide detectability evaluations. The fully documented pipeline is intended as a reproducible benchmark, while results on public tabular datasets indicate competitiveness beyond gravitational-wave applications. Although demonstrated for a fixed single-detector configuration, the construction supports extensions to detector networks and epoch-specific sensitivities. (Abridged)
